(b) A right angle is $90^{\circ}$. This angle is a little wider, so about $100^{\circ}$ is sensible.
These are estimates, not exact measurements.

It is wider than $90^{\circ}$ but smaller than $180^{\circ}$.
It is close to halfway between these benchmarks, $135^{\circ}$.
A sensible estimate is about $130^{\circ}$.

The angle is close to a straight angle, $180^{\circ}$, with a small gap.
It looks about $10^{\circ}$ smaller, so estimate about $170^{\circ}$.

The marked turn is more than three right angles, $270^{\circ}$, but less than a full turn, $360^{\circ}$.
It is a little more than $270^{\circ}$, so about $290^{\circ}$ is sensible.

(a) The marked turn is a little more than $270^{\circ}$ and well below $360^{\circ}$.
A sensible estimate is about $295^{\circ}$.
(b) $100^{\circ}$ is just beyond $90^{\circ}$. The $170^{\circ}$ estimate is close to a straight angle, so it is too large.

Turn the picture mentally so that one arm is horizontal. This does not change the size of the turn.

(a) Half a right angle is $45^{\circ}$. The marked angle looks about $10^{\circ}$ wider. To the nearest $10^{\circ}$, about $60^{\circ}$ is sensible.
(b) $40^{\circ}$ is a little less than $45^{\circ}$. The $80^{\circ}$ estimate is close to a whole right angle, so it is too large.
(c) Half a right angle is $45^{\circ}$. A sensible estimate is about $50^{\circ}$.

examples.derivation: (a) The arms have directions 0° and 56°, and the marked arc spans 56°. Half a right angle is 45°; the marked angle is 11° wider, consistent with the stated visual estimate of about 10° wider. Reporting about 60° to the nearest 10° is sensible. (b) 40° is 5° below 45°, whereas 80° is near 90°, so 40° matches the description. (c) 50° is 5° above 45°, making it a sensible example estimate. These comparisons use syllabus-supported benchmarks and remain within the accepted Stage 3 methods.
